one_month_reasoning: No Synopsys earnings in the window: Q4 FY26 results come in early December. The 30 Sep investor day (FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide $19.04-19.12, about 7% or more above the Street; ~$1B buyback) is already in the +12.8% move of 1 Oct. Events inside the window: TSMC Q3 results on Oct 15 (confirmed by TSMC IR; likely strong given the raised 2026 guide and N2 tape-out pace); Cadence Q3 results around Oct 26 (estimated, not yet confirmed), the closest peer read on EDA/IP demand and probably supportive given its $8.1B backlog; and the FOMC on Oct 27-28. The Fed hiked on Sep 16 and the dots imply one more 2026 hike, so a hawkish surprise is a two-sided risk to long-duration software multiples. The class-action response is due Nov 4, just outside the window. Short-horizon forces roughly offset: upward estimate revisions and the buyback support drift, while partial reversal after the gap day and the FOMC pull the other way. I set the median at ~$492 (flat), with a mixture of 80% at sigma 11% and 20% at sigma 20%. That is about 45%/3.5 with fatter tails for the FOMC and AI-disruption headlines like the July Kimi K3 sell-off. I left this ladder almost unchanged from round 1 except for slightly fatter tails.

fair_value.method: Blend of FY28E P/E (EPS $22.9 x 24x = $550, 50%), FY28E FCF yield ($20/sh at 3.8% = $526, 30%) and FY28E EV/sales (8.2x $12.7B = $104B EV less ~$5.0B net debt by Oct 2027 / 190M shares = $522, 20%), giving ~$537 for Oct 2027.

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 mid x 1.20. The company's mid-20s FY26-30 EPS CAGR implies ~23% after FY27; I haircut it to 20% for the 2025 IP miss (src 18). Peer growth (Cadence guide +19%, src 4; Siemens EDA revenue >30%, verified in transcript src 26) supports mid-teens revenue, but most of it is already in the FY27 guide, so I don't push above 20%.

Lowered from 25x. SNPS trades ~25.7x the FY27 guide vs CDNS ~41x forward (src 16, 17), but the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the dots show no 2027 cuts (src 22, 23), which caps re-rating of long-duration software. I keep a discount to CDNS for weaker IP share (CDNS IP +40% vs SNPS IP barely back to growth), Ansys leverage and China exposure.

Current EV/FY27 sales ~9.1x ($101.2B / $11.15B). I de-rate a little more than in round 1 (8.5x) for the rate backdrop.

10-Q: $10.04B debt less $3.61B cash = $6.4B (the supervisor's fact-check; I replaced the stockanalysis $7.2B, which includes leases). Less ~$3.9B FCF (Q4 FY26 plus FY27 $3.1B), plus ~$2.5B of buybacks ($1B accelerated plus about half of FY27 FCF), gives ~$5.0B.

bear.story: The 2025 pattern repeats: Design IP stalls again (Intel Foundry, China or custom-silicon slips; CDNS keeps taking IP share), Ansys slows, or EDA export controls to China (~10% of revenue) return. A second AI-disruption scare in the style of Kimi K3 meets a hawkish Fed. FY27 EPS comes in at $17.5-18 and the multiple drops to ~18-19x.

base.story: FY27 guide met or slightly beaten. The chain stays healthy (TSMC N2, hyperscaler custom silicon, Cadence and Siemens EDA growing), but that is mostly already in the guide. With rates higher for longer, the market prices FY28 EPS of ~$22.9 at ~24x.

bull.story: Agentic AI flows (GPT-Synopsys) lift EDA consumption, Amazon-style license-plus-royalty IP deals spread to other hyperscalers, margins head toward 50% early and the Fed pauses. The multiple re-rates toward ~29-30x FY28 EPS of ~$24.

thesis_break_reason: $370 is ~19.4x the freshly raised FY27 EPS guide and just above the 52-week low ($362.55), which was set during the Kimi K3 disruption scare and before the investor day. Trading there after a guide raise would mean the market rejects the FY27 numbers: most likely a new Design IP shortfall, renewed China EDA/IP export curbs, or a break in the AI design cycle across the chain (TSMC, Cadence). Lowered from $385 because the rate backdrop and documented ~8-9% one-day AI-scare drops mean ordinary volatility can reach the low $380s without anything fundamental going wrong.

Rate path: the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 with no cuts signalled for 2027, which caps multiple expansion for long-duration software

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor established three things I had missed or got wrong: (1) net debt is ~$6.4B per the 10-Q, not $7.2B; (2) the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with no 2027 cuts in the dots, which I verified with two independent press sources (src 22, 23); (3) my industry evidence (ESD +12.7%, Cadence +19%, TSMC N2) is mostly what the FY27 guide already embeds. I accept all three. I also verified the Kimi K3 shock (Yahoo, Jul 17 2026, SNPS/CDNS ~-9%; Bloomberg Intelligence sees no immediate threat because it is a 45nm proof of concept) and confirmed Siemens EDA revenue >30% in the Q3 call transcript (src 26), which settles the supervisor's 'unchecked' flag; that transcript also says EDA orders were 'softer as expected'. What goes beyond the guide: TSMC N2 tape-outs at 4x the N3 pace and hyperscaler custom silicon (the Amazon deal) argue for upside to FY28 rather than FY27, while CDNS/Siemens out-growing SNPS is a modest share warning. Changes: exit P/E 25x to 24x, FCF yield 3.6% to 3.8%, EV/sales 8.5x to 8.2x, net debt corrected. Fair value $562 to $537 (+9.5%). Scenarios are bear $335 (25%), base $545 (52%) and bull $700 (23%), mean ~$528. The ladder blends a three-lognormal scenario mixture (60%) with a single lognormal at median $515 and sigma 0.36 (40%) to respect the 45% realized vol, the de-rating history and AI-scare gaps. That gives P(>=spot) 0.60 (from 0.66) and a median of ~$532. I stay a little above the supervisor's 0.56 because the guide was just raised by 7%+, the chain data say demand is still accelerating at the leading edge, and a ~$1B buyback is near-term support; a hiking Fed lowers the multiple but does not cut the earnings path. The Wikipedia and Chinese-newsletter sources (14, 15) are narrative only and move no number. I did not look up option data or open priors/.
